3. Evolution algebras with given automorphism groups
  We now turn to the question of whether every finite group can be
the automorphism group of an evolution algebra.
Theorem 3.1. Let F be a field of characteristic 0. Given any finite
group G, there exists a finite dimensional idempotent evolution algebra
E over F such that Aut(E) ∼  = G.
Proof. A well-known result due to Frucht [9] says that for any finite
group G, there exists a graph Γ such that Aut(Γ) ∼= G. Suppose Γ has
n vertices. Let the adjacency matrix of Γ be B. For any nonnegative
integer x, set A(x) = B + xIn , where In is the identity matrix of size
n. Then for σ ∈ Sn ,
(3.1)            Pσ A(x) = A(x)Pσ ⇔ Pσ B = BPσ .
